improvements_over_revision_1: Seven of nine causal mutations were killed with passing controls.

failures.finding: The route reached explicit-human-approval but stopped before the frozen release-gate step, even though the evaluation asks for the complete intended route rather than execution.
failures.required_revision: State structurally that complete route planning includes the post-decision release-gate while execution still stops for the named human decision.

failures.finding: The router selected tool-runtime-readiness because setup authorization was absent, although the frozen routing fixture asks which atomic capability owns a missing project-local test runtime.
failures.required_revision: Separate target ownership from activation: route to test-runtime-bootstrap, mark activation needs-input/disabled until fresh authorization, and never execute from routing.

failures.finding: The mutant changed permission identity and mutation scope but retained hard Gates forbidding repair; the behavioral assertion did not name the immutable expected identity/scope, so the model reasonably treated the mutated values as exact.
failures.required_revision: Use a causal mutant that also removes non-remediation Gates and asks review to fix source, and name the expected original identity/scope in the challenge.

failures.finding: The control requires human acceptance of release scope and residual risk but does not require a named decision owner, so the predeclared named-human challenge correctly failed.
failures.required_revision: Add a named human release decision owner and durable decision evidence to the revised delivery composite; generate the mutant from that revised control.
